- Claude Code conducted a full market analysis, identifying ~4,000 coffee shops in Washington (57.3 per 100k, 2nd highest in US), with ~1,800 addressable independents in the Puget Sound corridor after filtering franchises.

- Analysis revealed three major obstacles: free training bundled into wholesale roaster contracts (competitors like Caffe Vita, US Roast), Seattle Barista Academy charging $1,050–$1,200/day with institutional credibility, and weak buyer economics (2.5–7% net margins, 50–74% failure rate within five years).

- Key finding: the PNW drive-thru market doesn't reward coffee quality improvements—sugar, fat, and temperature mask extraction differences, so customers won't pay premium for better coffee. Revenue lift is unmeasurable, eliminating ROI story needed for sales.

- Ceiling on consulting model: ~$60–75k net per person annually, no recurring revenue, no asset value. Business model does not scale.

- Two scalable alternative pivots recommended: (A) sell training to roasters as their outsourced training arm (one sale reaches 30–80 stands), (B) monthly espresso calibration/PM route as recurring service ($200/stand × 60 = $12k MRR, same structure as Got Moles).

- Deliverables: full market analysis PDF saved to `C:\Users\spenc\Downloads\Coffee-Consulting-Market-Analysis.pdf` and project folder `projects/str-market-analysis/`; includes a 30-day validation test with preset decision rules.
